findings.title: Passing raw componentClass drops parameterized component type for generic arrays
findings.description: In the `GenericArrayType` branch, `componentType` is the *declared* generic component type (e.g. `List<String>` for a `List<String>[]` field), while `componentClass` is reduced to the raw class via `TypeUtils.getClass(componentType)` (line 170). After this change the raw class is handed to `DefaultJSONParser.parseArray`, so element deserialization no longer receives the parameterized type. For a field declared as `List<String>[]` or `Map<String,Bean>[]`, elements will now be deserialized using the raw `List`/`Map` type, i.e. nested values become untyped `JSONObject`/`JSONArray`/`Integer` instances instead of the declared element types (`String`, `Bean`, ...). Consumers that later read those typed values will observe changed runtime types and can hit `ClassCastException`. The pre-change code preserved the full `Type` for element parsing (`parser.parseArray(componentType, array, fieldName)`); only the `TypeVariable` sub-case benefits from the substitution (the resolved `Class` is a valid parser input there).
evidence: ObjectArrayCodec.java:143-145 - `if (type instanceof GenericArrayType) { GenericArrayType clazz = (GenericArrayType) type; componentType = clazz.getGenericComponentType();` (componentType keeps the declared generic component type)
ObjectArrayCodec.java:169-171 - `} else { componentClass = TypeUtils.getClass(componentType); }` (componentClass is the raw class, losing type arguments of a ParameterizedType)
ObjectArrayCodec.java:174 - `componentType = componentClass = clazz.getComponentType();` (only in the plain-Class branch are the two values identical, so this branch is unaffected)
ObjectArrayCodec.java:177 (changed line) - `parser.parseArray(componentClass, array, fieldName);` now uses the raw class instead of the declared `Type` for element parsing
ObjectArrayCodec.java:179 - `return (T) toObjectArray(parser, componentClass, array);` shows the array is cast using the raw class as well, so generic information is discarded end-to-end

findings.title: Change only rewires the component type argument; no input validation added for the CVE-2017-18349 (CWE-20) surface
findings.description: The MR is the only change in the diff and it merely swaps which `Type`/`Class` object is passed to `DefaultJSONParser.parseArray`. It adds no validation or rejection of untrusted input and does not alter any class-instantiation/autoType gate (no changes in `ParserConfig` or `DefaultJSONParser`). For the ordinary array cases the change is a no-op because `componentType` and `componentClass` are the same object (line 174), so `Object[]` and concrete bean arrays follow exactly the same deserialization path as before. Worse, in the `TypeVariable` branch the resolved type falls back to `Object.class` whenever the actual type argument is not itself a `Class` (line 164), so elements are then parsed with the least-restrictive component type. Therefore this hunk does not by itself constitute a mitigation for the autoType-driven arbitrary-instantiation weakness described by CVE-2017-18349; reviewers should confirm that the actual autoType restriction lives elsewhere (e.g. a `ParserConfig` allow/deny check), which is absent from this diff.
evidence: Diff contains exactly one hunk, in ObjectArrayCodec.java line 177; no other file is modified, so no validation/autoType policy code is added

ObjectArrayCodec.java:174 - `componentType = componentClass = clazz.getComponentType();` proves the new argument is identical to the old one for the plain-Class array case, so that path is not hardened

ObjectArrayCodec.java:161-165 - `if (actualType instanceof Class) { componentClass = (Class) actualType; } else { componentClass = Object.class; }` falls back to `Object.class`, the most permissive component type
Symbol lookup for `checkAutoType` over all Java sources returns 0 matches, indicating no autoType guard is reachable from this code path in the snapshot

findings.title: `componentType` becomes a dead assignment in the plain-Class branch
findings.description: After the change, both `parser.parseArray(...)` (line 177) and `toObjectArray(...)` (line 179) use `componentClass`. In the non-generic branch the statement `componentType = componentClass = clazz.getComponentType();` (line 174) therefore assigns `componentType` a value that is never read on that path, which obscures the actual data flow and makes the distinction between the two variables (declared `Type` vs resolved `Class`) easy to get wrong in future edits.
evidence: ObjectArrayCodec.java:142 - `Type componentType;` declared and only needed for the GenericArrayType branch after this change
ObjectArrayCodec.java:174 - `componentType = componentClass = clazz.getComponentType();` assigns componentType which is no longer consumed in this branch
ObjectArrayCodec.java:177 and 179 - both consumers now take `componentClass`, leaving `componentType` unused on the plain-Class path
